四级汇总词汇 · 37英文原文

The Line the River Had Moved

被河水挪动的那条线 · 640 词 · 8 段 · 首次出现的目标词加粗

1An earthquake shocked a remote village beside a dam. No house collapsed, but a geological survey found a long crack. News of a deadly flood spread through the northwestern district. A terrified parent reported that the dam had failed. The message came from a family approximately a kilometer away. Sal, a teacher, asked a team to investigate before people scattered. A swift decision mattered, yet nobody knew the actual impact or which route might endanger them.

2A geological worker drove from the northeastern district after a violent shower. A blizzard the previous winter had buried a survey post near the dam. During a week of sunshine the snow melted, and runoff cut a narrow gap across the slope. The quake had then disturbed the loosened soil. A muddy block began to slide into the river. It had not yet reached the dam. The worker marked a hazard boundary where falling soil might reach a road if the ground became saturated again.

3The boundary appeared to cross an empty field. A farmer remembered a road used by market traders throughout summer. A picturesque row of houses now stood beyond it. A storm had torn out a culvert and changed the route of water. The official map did not show that deterioration. The village's vulnerability came from one narrow road as much as from a possible collapse. Sal asked a surveyor to add every building near that part of the river.

4A drill had taught the pupils to gather at a gym on low ground. That route crossed the hazard boundary. In a rapid evacuation, a crowd might crush someone at the narrow bridge. Sal asked the head teacher to walk a second route with her. They found a broad path behind a chapel. Its surface was shaky near a ditch, but a farmer had dug a solid exit above the wet patch. The team could adjust the route without asking people to climb the unstable slope.

5A thunderous shower brought hail and poor visibility. A driver tried to turn through the wrong gate. Sal used a printed photo to direct him uphill. A volunteer placed bright cloth at the turn. Amidst the chaos, a shivering child asked how far he had to walk. Another volunteer told him where to stop if he felt exhaustion. The worst of the rush eased once people could see a route. They no longer had to wait helplessly near the river.

6A massive block of soil slid into the river during the night. Its swell covered the old lane and contaminated a water tank. The dam stayed intact. The team discussed sustaining families after the closure. Immense damage was still possible. No fatality had been reported. Still, poor access to water could become a tremendous burden. The report marked that difference and described the most likely hazard instead of repeating a rumor.

7The village had a second concern. A stream above the damaged tank had picked up mud from a partial collapse. Nobody wanted polluted water to add to the misery. A neighboring district offered a temporary supply. Sal asked the team to show where collection would occur. With rumors still causing confusion, a clear address mattered as much as a warning about a possible disaster.

8A child asked if the warning line would stay put. Sal laid the old map under a transparent sheet. A raging stream had crossed the route in one place, but a different disturbance could close another part. An ecological problem might persist even if that disaster never occurred. The class marked two ways out. Misunderstanding the boundary could split a group. They rehearsed with one person who checked the rear. That visible plan did more than a frightening announcement. It helped the children explain why a disastrous outcome was less likely if they recognized the first sign and left together.

四级汇总词汇 · 37中文译文

被河水挪动的那条线

按英文段落顺序对照阅读

1一场地震惊动了水坝旁的偏远村庄。没有房屋倒塌，但地质勘查发现一条很长的裂缝。致命洪水要来的消息传遍了西北片区。一位惊慌的家长说，水坝已经垮了。消息来自约一公里外的一户人家。教师萨尔请工作队先去核实，免得大家慌乱四散。必须迅速作决定，但当时没人知道地震究竟造成了什么影响，也不知道哪条路会有危险。

2一阵暴雨过后，地质人员从东北片区开车过来。前一年的暴风雪埋住了水坝附近一根测量标杆。一周晴天让雪融化，地表径流在坡上冲出一道窄沟，地震随后震松了那片土。一大块泥土开始滑向河里，还没到水坝。工作人员划出危险边界，说明如果地面再次吸饱水，滑落的土可能在哪一段冲上公路。

3从地图上看，这道边界只穿过一片空地。一位农民记得，夏天赶集的人一直走那条路。路外如今还多了一排好看的房子。一场暴风雨冲毁了涵洞，也改变了水流方向，正式地图上却看不出这些变化。村子之所以容易受困，既是因为可能发生坍塌，也是因为只有一条窄路可走。萨尔请测量员把河段附近的每栋房屋都补上。

4学生们在演习中学的是到低处的体育馆集合，那条路线却穿过危险区。紧急撤离时，人多起来，可能会有人在窄桥上被挤伤。萨尔请校长和她走一遍另一条路线。他们在小教堂后找到一条宽路。靠近沟渠的地面不稳，不过一位农民已在湿地上方挖出一个结实的出口。这样，队伍就能改走新路，大家也不用爬那片不稳的坡。

5一阵带雷声的急雨打下来，还夹着冰雹，视线很差。一位司机差点拐进错误的大门。萨尔拿一张印出来的照片给他指明上坡的方向。志愿者在转弯处挂了一块鲜艳的布。混乱中，一个发抖的孩子问还要走多远。另一位志愿者告诉他，要是累了，可以在哪里停。大家一看清路线，最慌乱的时候就过去了。他们终于可以离开河边。

6夜里，一大块土滑入河中。涌起的水淹没了老路，污染了一个储水箱，水坝仍然完好。工作队讨论封路后怎样维持各户的生活。严重损失仍有可能，当时也还没有收到死亡报告。可供水不畅已经可能给村子带来沉重负担。报告把这几件事分别写清楚，指出最可能发生的危险，把未经核实的消息留了出去。

7村里还有另一个问题。受损水箱上游的一条小溪已经被局部坍塌的泥土弄浑。谁都不想再让污染水源加重困难。邻近片区愿意临时供水。萨尔请工作队写清取水地点。谣言还在造成混乱，这时，一个明确的地址和灾害警报同样重要。

8一个孩子问，警戒线会不会一直在原处。萨尔把旧地图放在透明薄片下面。急流这一次从一个地方冲过道路，下一次的变化可能封住另一段。即使最严重的灾害没发生，生态问题也可能持续。全班标出了两条出路。弄错危险边界可能让队伍走散，于是他们排练了一次，指定一人负责照看队尾。大家看得见的路线比吓人的通告管用。孩子们自己也能说清，早点认出征兆，再一起离开，为什么更能避开危险。
